extra/agent_loop.txt.title: The run's guardrails
note: **Decides what this run is allowed to do, before it starts.**
- `allowed_tools`: pre-approved, so these never stop to ask
- `max_turns`: the loop's hard stop — the CLI's `--max-turns`

extra/agent_loop.txt.anchor: async for message in query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
extra/agent_loop.txt.title: The message loop
note: **Reads what the agent streams back and prints it as it happens.**
- Text blocks are Claude talking; tool blocks are Claude acting
- The final message carries turns, duration, and the answer

extra/auto_agent.txt.title: What's about to run
note: **Pulls out the tool's name and, for Bash, the actual command string.**
- Reading the arguments is the whole point: `ls` and `rm -rf` are both Bash

extra/auto_agent.txt.anchor: if tool_name == "Bash" and ("rm " in command or "sudo" in command):
extra/auto_agent.txt.title: The one refusal
note: **Refuses any Bash command carrying `rm ` or `sudo`.**
- `"deny"` stops the call before it runs
- The reason is sent back to Claude so it can adapt

extra/auto_agent.txt.title: The default answer
note: **Everything else is allowed — and printed, so you can see what ran.**
- No branch returns "ask": there is nobody here to answer one

extra/auto_agent.txt.title: Settings, then the run
note: **The tools this job needs, a turn cap, and your gate wired in.**
- `matcher=None` means the hook sees *every* tool call
- Note Bash is absent from `allowed_tools` — step 9 relies on that

extra/project_server.txt.title: Tool 1 — run the test suite
note: **Runs `app/test_app.py` and hands the pass/fail output back to Claude.**
- The docstring is the tool's description — it's how Claude decides to call it
- Returns plain text, exit code included

extra/project_server.txt.title: Tool 2 — count the TODOs
note: **Counts TODO/FIXME comments across the repo's `.py` and `.js` files.**
- The `skip` set keeps `.venv` and `node_modules` out of the total

extra/project_server.txt.title: Tool 3 — size and shape
note: **Files and line counts per file type — a quick read on the codebase.**
- Same pattern as the other two: plain function in, MCP tool out
